answer: Before a new account opens, it must pass one narrow inlet: a fresh puzzle tied to its own key, a ferrous-hard computation an ordinary laptop solves in minutes, yielding one signed proof. Two nodes check the signature and hash within ten minutes; a missing, copied, or reused proof means the account never opens, and a second account with the same proof is refused outright. One honest agent picks up its quill once and signs one proof, while 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000 separate puzzles, so a farm reusing one solution stalls at the second account.
